title: Lane Johnson, long-time Eagles star RT, says he’s likely to retire after 2026 season
content:
Lane Johnson, the Philadelphia Eagles’ All-Pro right tackle, said on Saturday that the 2026 NFL season will “probably” be his last.

Johnson, 36, said family has become more of a priority in his life than football. He reached this decision about his future while recently spending four practices away from the Eagles’ facility with an excused absence. He said his mother is “struggling with some health stuff.” He also mentioned his father and that his oldest child, David, is soon turning 13.

“As you get older, things change in your life: Priorities. Your children get older, parents get older,” said Johnson, who is entering his 14th NFL season since the Eagles selected him with the fourth pick of the 2013 NFL Draft. “It just puts things into perspective. Looking like this is probably, potentially, going to be my last year. … I had gotten to that point of those priorities away from football are starting to merge. … I thought about it last year. Not that I don’t enjoy it; I love everything about this game and preparing for it. But that’s where I’m at in my career.”

Johnson considered retirement in the offseason for similar reasons, he said, but not while he was away during his four-day training camp absence.

“The plan was always to come back,” Johnson said.

The tackle said he felt good returning to practice on Friday and “picked up where I left off.” He thanked the organization for its support. Former teammate Jason Kelce, who attended both practices, stood at the back of the media tent while Johnson spoke. Eagles owner Jeffrey Lurie spent a few minutes speaking with Johnson after Saturday’s practice.

“I’m here, my team’s supporting me. I’m where I need to be,” Johnson said. “But yeah, I’ve had conversations with family members. You can’t play forever. Not everybody can do what LeBron James is doing. I am 36. It is weird to say. All the love, all the support here. Yeah, man, I plan on having a really good last year.”

Johnson is one of the most accomplished players in Eagles history, and his accolades may one day pave a path to Canton. He started on both of the franchise’s Super Bowl teams in 2017 and 2024; he was named a first-team All-Pro twice, a second-team All-Pro three times and a Pro Bowler six times.

Johnson has also been one of the most outspoken members of the Eagles about his excitement for first-time offensive coordinator Sean Mannion’s zone blocking-oriented system. He believes he can conclude his career with one more great season.

“I still feel like I can be a premier tackle in this league,” Johnson said.

The Eagles, aware of Johnson’s age and considerations, spent a third-round pick on Miami’s Markel Bell to potentially become Johnson’s successor. Bell spent the majority of the week with the first-team offense at right tackle in Johnson’s absence.

“He’s one of the best rookies I’ve been around,” Johnson said of Bell. “Just as far as being in the playbook, no complaining. Haven’t heard him complain one time. He’s always asking questions. Just a really mature young man who handles stuff off the field well. He’s just always asking questions. You can tell he was coached up well at Miami. Yeah, man, when I see a guy with that size and that ability and that wing span and movement, you can have a lot of success in this business.”
